title: [AUG-125] Dual-track sessions: correct duration and much faster local whisper transcription (retranscription of failed recordings)
why_we_need_this:
Retranscribing a failed dual-track session is a normal recovery flow ("Transcribe again"), but today it behaves badly and misleads the user.

Reference case: session `a49e4b18-b0f8-4ecc-86f6-6d34af0e2020` (@server/data/sessions/a49e4b18-b0f8-4ecc-86f6-6d34af0e2020/session.json), status `failed` ("Transcription cancelled by user"), `dualTrack: true`, `systemOffsetMs: -334`.
Measured with ffprobe (all 16 kHz mono PCM):
- `audio-mic.wav` / `audio-mic-boosted.wav` = 971.7 s (16:11)
- `audio-system.wav` / `audio-system-boosted.wav` = 3257.2 s (54:17)

Observed problems:
1. Wrong duration in UI. TranscriptView header (@client/src/components/TranscriptView.tsx ~line 401-420, `.transcript-circuit-meta`) shows 00:16:11. That is only the mic track. `session.duration` and `estimatedDuration` are computed from the mic WAV only in both the upload path and the retranscribe path (@server/src/routes/sessions.ts ~lines 305-312 and 418-424: `getAudioDuration(micWav)`). The system ("Them") track is 3.35x longer, so the real call length and the ETA (1720 s) are both false.
2. Retranscription is very slow and the progress/ETA does not reflect the real work: whisper processes 54 min of system audio + 16 min of mic, while the estimate is based on 16 min. Boosted WAVs are regenerated on every retry (new mtimes) even though they already exist.
3. The mic/system length mismatch itself is suspicious (mic stopped ~38 min before system capture ended, or system capture was not stopped with the recording). Root cause must be identified: either the mic MediaRecorder died / was truncated, or server-side system capture (AUG-113 "System" source) kept running after stop.

Without a fix users see a false duration, cannot predict how long recovery takes, and may lose the "Them" or "Me" part of a real call.

## Performance: August vs SplitVox (reference implementation)
The same local model processes audio much faster in the sibling Praxis project SplitVox (/Users/rugarov/git/SplitVox, see its project-context/transcription/README.md and app/Sources/SplitVoxTranscription/WhisperTranscriber.swift ~lines 150-260). August's pipeline (@server/src/services/whisper.ts ~line 328 `runWhisper` args, @server/src/routes/sessions.ts `runDualTranscription` ~line 80-100) differs in these measurable ways:

| Aspect | SplitVox | August today |
|---|---|---|
| Decoding strategy | Explicit GREEDY. Comment: "BEAM_SEARCH (beam 5) was measured 1.6-3.4x slower" and did not improve quality | No `--beam-size` / `--best-of` passed → whisper-cli CLI defaults to beam search (beam 5, best-of 5) — likely the single biggest slowdown |
| Stream concurrency | Mic then system run **sequentially** through ONE whisper context ("only one Metal context should be active") | `Promise.all([transcribe(mic), transcribe(system)])` → two whisper-cli processes at once, each with `--threads cpu-1` (`threadCount()`), i.e. 2×(N-1) CPU threads + two Metal/Vulkan contexts competing for one GPU |
| Model load | Model loaded once, reused for both streams | Each whisper-cli process loads the model from disk separately |
| Silence handling | Leading silence trimmed before decode (window RMS < 0.01, 1 s windows); timestamps shifted back by the trimmed offset | Every second of silence is decoded (a 54-min system track in a call is largely silence) |
| Context | `n_max_text_ctx = 0`, `no_context = true` | `--max-context 0` (equivalent — keep) |
| Model | ggml-large-v3-turbo (f16), Metal | ggml-large-v3-turbo-q8_0 (@server/src/config.ts:117); on Metal q8_0 is not guaranteed faster than f16 — must be benchmarked, not assumed |
| Threads | `activeProcessorCount - 1` for one job | Same formula but per process, doubled by parallelism |

whisper.cpp also offers built-in VAD (`--vad` + Silero VAD model, whisper.cpp ≥ 1.7.6) that skips non-speech regions entirely and flash attention (`--flash-attn`, check default for the pinned version) — both are candidates to evaluate.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Root cause of the mic (16:11) vs system (54:17) length mismatch for session a49e4b18 is identified and documented (client MediaRecorder truncation, crash-recovery blob, or system capture not stopped); if it is a capture/recording bug, it is fixed so both tracks end at the same stop moment (±2 s) on macOS and Windows.
- [ ] For dual-track sessions, `session.duration` = max(mic duration, system duration + systemOffsetMs) in upload, retranscribe and completion paths; the TranscriptView header shows the real call length (54:17 for the reference session, not 16:11).
- [ ] Baseline benchmark recorded BEFORE changes: wall-clock time to transcribe the reference session (copy) with current args, on this Mac (Apple Silicon, Metal); result written into the task notes / project-context.
- [ ] whisper-cli is invoked with explicit greedy decoding (`--beam-size 1 --best-of 1` or equivalent), matching SplitVox; transcript quality on the reference session is spot-checked against the baseline output (no loss of Me/Them utterances, no repetition loops).
- [ ] Dual-track transcription runs mic and system **sequentially** (or through a single shared whisper worker), never two GPU-backed whisper-cli processes at once; thread count is chosen for one active job. Applies to both upload and retranscribe paths; live transcription is not slowed down or blocked.
- [ ] Non-speech audio is not decoded: either whisper.cpp built-in VAD (`--vad` with a bundled/auto-downloaded Silero model, available on macOS and Windows builds) or a leading/long-silence trim like SplitVox; all segment timestamps stay on the original track timeline so mergeDualStream alignment (systemOffsetMs) is unchanged.
- [ ] Model choice (large-v3-turbo f16 vs q8_0) and `--flash-attn` are benchmarked on the reference session on macOS; the faster option with equal quality is used; decision and numbers documented. Windows (Vulkan / CPU fallback) path is not regressed.
- [ ] After changes, full transcription of the reference session (≈70 min of audio total) is at least 3x faster than the recorded baseline on the same Mac; exact before/after numbers reported.
- [ ] `estimatedDuration` for dual-track sessions is calculated from the actual work (both tracks, new pipeline speed), so the ETA/progress shown during retranscription is within ±25% of the real processing time for the reference session.
- [ ] Retranscribing the reference session produces a completed transcript containing both [Me] and [Them] utterances, with Them utterances covering the full system track (last Them utterance end ≈ 54 min), correctly aligned by systemOffsetMs.
- [ ] Retranscribe does not needlessly redo work: existing `audio-*.wav` conversions are reused, and boosted WAVs are reused when the source file is unchanged (or regeneration is justified in the task notes).
- [ ] If a track is significantly longer than the other (>10% or >60 s), the server logs a warning and the UI surfaces it non-blockingly (e.g. "Mic track is shorter than system audio") instead of silently showing one duration.
- [ ] Cancelling and then retranscribing a failed session works repeatedly without leftover whisper processes or stale status (verified by cancel → retranscribe → complete).
- [ ] Type check / build pass for client and server; changes verified on macOS, Windows path handling and whisper-cli.exe args reviewed; @project-context/transcription/README.md updated with the duration, whisper parameters, benchmark numbers and retranscription rules.
important_constraints:
- Both platforms (macOS and Windows) must be supported; no platform-specific assumptions in paths, ffmpeg/whisper invocation or capture stop logic. Any new asset (e.g. VAD model) must be downloaded/bundled by `npm run setup` and the DMG / Windows build on both platforms.
- Keep the existing GPU fallback logic (gpuBackend.ts, Vulkan --no-gpu retry, AUG-117) intact.
- Keep `--max-context 0` (anti repetition-loop, same as SplitVox `n_max_text_ctx = 0`).
- SplitVox is a reference only: do not copy its Swift in-process architecture or modify the SplitVox repo; port the parameters and ideas into August's whisper-cli pipeline.
- Do not delete or modify the original audio files of the reference session; copy it to a scratch session for experiments.
- Keep the existing API contract (POST /api/sessions/:id/retranscribe, session.json fields); new fields must be optional and backward compatible with existing sessions.
- Single-track sessions must keep working (they benefit from the new whisper args but their flow is unchanged).
- Post-recording transcription stays local whisper only (no Groq).
- Do not reintroduce auto-deletion of sessions (removed in AUG-121).
